title: Nvidia Stock (NVDA) Falls 3.9% as AI Stocks Retreat (Nov 25)
summary: NVDA fell 3.91% to $149.30 on Nov 25 as AI-linked stocks slid after hot October PCE inflation data. What drove Nvidia's drop, plus key risks.
body_markdown:
## Why Nvidia Stock Fell


No new Nvidia announcement was reported behind Wednesday's decline. Financial media tied it to a broader sell-off in AI stocks: according to[The Motley Fool's market recap](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/11/25/stock-market-today-nov-25-nvidia-slides-3-9-as-the-market-considers-hot-pce-inflation-data-and-new-tariff-proposals/) , investors sold AI-linked stocks on renewed worries about spending, higher rates and[inflation](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-inflation-affects-investing-risk-types-real-returns/) . New tariff proposals added to the pressure, the recap said, without detailing them.


The inflation figure came from the[US Bureau of Economic Analysis](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/personal-income-and-outlays-october-2026) , which reported Wednesday morning that the PCE price index rose 3.8% in October from a year earlier and 0.3% from September. The Motley Fool noted that the headline reading was in line with estimates but nearly twice the Federal Reserve's target, making another rate hike seem more likely to investors. The US 10-year Treasury yield closed the session at 4.85%, down 6.0 basis points.


[A separate Motley Fool analysis](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/25/why-nvidia-stock-is-falling-again/) also pointed to debt worries, reporting that credit default swap spreads, the cost of insuring debt, hit record highs over the past two sessions for companies across the AI trade, including Alphabet, Oracle, SpaceX and CoreWeave, which the outlet described as some of Nvidia's biggest customers.


The sell-off came two days after Nvidia's board[reinstated Jensen Huang](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-board-reinstates-jensen-huang-as-president-ceo-and-board-director) as president, CEO and board director, effective immediately, on November 23. The market recap said investors are weighing his return against ongoing risks tied to investigations into his actions and the company's export controls.


## NVDA Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Leadership: according to Nvidia, its board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang and, after input from senior levels of the US government, is confident his return poses no national security risk.
- Growth: per[The Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/25/anthropic-s-chip-choices-could-change-the-nvidia-story-here-s-how/) , third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue rose 103% to $115.8 billion and[earnings per share](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/what-is-eps-earnings-per-share-meaning-formula-and-how-to-judge-it/) rose 111% to $2.68.
- Demand: Anthropic's S-1 filing shows Nvidia GPUs supply up to 4.7 gigawatts of its compute, about 42% of its total capacity, as reported by The Motley Fool.


### Risks


- Investigations: Nvidia said an independent-director committee's probe into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort will proceed to conclusion, and that it will keep cooperating with government inquiries.
- Competition: Anthropic is spreading its chip spending across Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon and AMD, and The Motley Fool cited estimates that put Nvidia's share of AI accelerators at 75% this year, down from 80% to 90% last year.
- Margins: Nvidia said fourth-quarter gross margins will be between 71% and 72%, down from nearly 75% in the third quarter, mostly because of rising memory costs, according to The Motley Fool.
